Thank you for taking the time to leave feedback for the practice, I am sorry o hear you are unhappy with the service. 
With regards to the wait time, unfortunately on occasion a wait does occur, this can be due to many reasons, an emergency in the previous appointments which causes delay, IT issues, patients having multiple concerns to discuss (which we encourage more than one appointment for). The clinicians do try to run to time but this is not always possible, the reception team are encouraged to make the patients aware that there may be a delay when they check in, I am sorry if this did not occur when you arrived. 
We are a large practice and do have multiple clinicians who will be able to review prior to consultation, if you do have a preferred clinician it is possible to request this when arranging an appointment. 
With regards to appointment waiting times, we are a busy practice but access is reviewed regularly to ensure appointments are available for patients when they ring, we do have busier days and appointments may go quicker, all reception staff are trained in Care Navigation and may be in a position to direct you to an alternative service such as the pharmacy, physio, etc depending on presenting complaint. 
Should you wish to discuss this further please do not hesitate to contact the practice and arrange a suitable time to discuss. 
Many Thanks

There was a form we were going to bring that assists the appointment and the GP to assess these symptoms and it is by all accounts the starting point for what is a complicated and complex journey for people experiencing ADHD.

You on about?”. The whole experience was dreadful. No compassion, no professionalism, no willingness to assist, it felt as though she had prejudged me and my partner by wanting to discuss ADHD symptoms. So we are no further forward, can’t even get past the receptionist to start this process. Her advice to drop the form off at reception was incorrect. The purpose of this form (Right to Choose) was to bring into the appointment for your GP to discuss with you, and to then begin the process of being referred for diagnosis in the first instance.
